title: Build an image from rgba values

seo.metaTitle: RGB Values to PNG - Free Image Builder, Nothing Uploaded
seo.metaDescription: Assemble an image from rgba(r, g, b, a) numbers: paste the list, set the width, the height is computed automatically. Free, private, runs in your browser.
seo.longDescription: Building an image from rgba values is the reverse of listing one: you have a run of numbers in the CSS spelling of a color - rgba(255, 0, 0, 255) and its neighbours - and want them back as a picture. Paste the values into the text field, set Width to the number of pixels in one row, and the height follows from the total, so a 32 by 32 icon is 256 rgba groups at a width of 32. Commas, parentheses and line breaks are ignored, which means a list copied out of a stylesheet works as it is, but the values are not negotiable: each must be a whole number from 0 to 255, four per pixel, and the pixel count must divide evenly by the width. A wrong width is the one mistake the page cannot detect - it assembles a sheared picture without complaining.
howTo: Paste the rgba(255, 0, 0, 255) style values into the text field; the punctuation is ignored.
Set Width to the pixel count of a single row - divide the value count by four to get the pixel count, then check that it divides evenly.
Compare the preview with the shape you expect and change the width if rows are offset.
Download the assembled PNG from the Download button.

faq.q: Do the parentheses and commas have to be exact?
faq.a: No, only the numbers are read. Spacing, commas, parentheses and line breaks are ignored, so a stylesheet rule pastes fine.

faq.q: Why does an error appear when the numbers do not fit?
faq.a: A partial row has no sensible answer, so a remainder is reported with both numbers rather than padded away.
No. Every channel is a byte between 0 and 255, and fractions are rejected. Multiply a CSS alpha such as 0.5 by 255 before pasting.

faq.q: Where do I get this format?
faq.a: From an image: the PNG to RGB values tool prints every pixel in this exact notation, one image row per line, an exact round trip in pixel values.
